claims.statement: The CodeWriter class uses a linkedHashMap called importableTypes to memoize simple-name-to-fully-qualified-name mappings for types that cannot be resolved through existing imports, nesting context, or same-package scope.

The lookupName method resolves type names by walking outward from the target class through its enclosing classes, checking at each level whether a local simple name matches via imported types and nesting context.
The typeSpecStack is a mutable builder list that tracks the current nesting context during code emission, enabling scope-aware resolution of nested types.

Import suggestion generation uses a two-pass algorithm: the first pass collects candidates during traversal, and the second pass filters out same-package references via referencedNames to produce final suggestions.
The LineWrapper class implements soft-wrapping on an appendable by buffering characters until a line wrap is needed, then emitting a newline followed by indentation based on the current indent level.
The wrappingSpace method defers emission of either a literal space or a newline-plus-indent sequence until the next flush, using an enum FlushType to track the deferred action.

The zeroWidthSpace method defers a line break (no newline or space) when the current column is non-zero, ensuring logical content that doesn't naturally span multiple lines still gets readable breaks.

The emitAndIndent method emits indentation lazily only at line boundaries to avoid trailing whitespace on wrapped lines, and handles comment prefixes for Javadoc (" * ") versus single-line comments ("/\/ ").

The statementLine field tracks whether the current line is part of a multi-line statement; when it reaches zero after incrementing, indent increases by 2 to establish double-indentation for continuations.
The suggestedImports method returns a linkedHashMap of types that need import statements by copying importableTypes and removing any names present in referencedNames (same-package references).
